description: Use this when building or revising an eval set, LLM-as-judge prompt or rubric, and you need the user's own judgment on example outputs. Send the rubric and 1 to 50 cases (input, output, optional context, optional verdict and reason from your own judge). Returns a review link for the user, a review id and a read token. Show the link to the user and ask them to grade, then call wait_for_human_review with the id and token. Your judge verdicts are hidden from the user until they grade each case, so their call is not anchored on yours. For a follow-up round after revising the rubric, pass parent_id with the previous review id.

cases.description: 1 to 50 cases. Pick the ones you are least sure about.

context.description: Optional: retrieved docs, tool results, or the expected answer.

input.description: What the user said, or the task given to the system under test.

judge_verdict.description: Optional: your LLM judge's verdict on this case.

parent_id.description: The previous review id, when this is a revised round.

product.description: One line on the system under test, e.g. "Support bot for a bike shop".

rubric.description: The current rubric, one rule per entry. May be empty if you want the user to grade from instinct first.

title.description: Short name for this batch, e.g. "Refund agent evals, round 1".

name: request_human_review
title: Ask the user to grade eval cases
